name: Mangrove
description: Boundary ecosystem at land-sea edge. Ultrafiltration root membranes exclude 90% of salt. Aerial prop roots create 3D habitat architecture for thousands of species. Viviparous propagules germinate while attached, dropping as ready-to-root seedlings.

core_attributes.pattern: boundary ecosystem engineering, salt ultrafiltration, aerial root architecture

scope.definition: Carbon sequestration rate efficiency of mangrove ecosystems — ratio of mangrove 'blue carbon' storage per hectare per year to equivalent tropical rainforest carbon storage on per-area basis.

evidence.source: Donato et al. (2011) 'Mangroves among the most carbon-rich forests in the tropics', Nature Geoscience 4:293-297; McLeod et al. (2011) 'A blueprint for blue carbon', Frontiers in Ecology.
cross_domain_examples: mangrove soil carbon density 1023 Mg C/ha — 3-5× higher than tropical upland forest
mangrove carbon burial rate 174 g C/m²/year — 50× faster than upland forest soil carbon accumulation
saltmarsh blue carbon: analogous coastal ecosystem with 250 g C/m²/year burial — same tidal anoxia mechanism
seagrass meadows: third blue carbon ecosystem type with 83 g C/m²/year sediment burial

scope.falsifiability: If isotope dating of mangrove sediment cores shows carbon burial rates <50 g C/m²/year over 100-year averages, the exceptional blue carbon storage rate is not sustained.
scope.measurement_limits: Carbon sequestration rate is tide-regime dependent — high tidal flushing reduces anaerobic sediment accretion. Deforested mangroves release stored carbon rapidly (years vs centuries for terrestrial soils).
